findings.claim: In the AQA English Literature exam, Animal Farm questions always ask you to write about both what happens in the text and how Orwell presents ideas.
findings.truth: The board must never be named in student-facing text. The rest of the sentence is right.
findings.evidence: house rule: no board name in lesson text

findings.claim: Remember: AQA awards marks for how well you link methods to meaning, not just for feature-spotting.
findings.truth: Same rule: the board must not be named. The claim itself is right.
findings.evidence: house rule: no board name in lesson text

findings.claim: For extract-based questions, start with close analysis of the given passage before widening to the whole text.
findings.truth: There is no extract for a modern prose or drama text. The exam is closed book and the student answers one essay question from a choice of two on the whole text. Telling a student to start from a printed passage teaches the wrong exam.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md, Specification at a glance: 'All assessments are closed book'; Paper 2 Section A 'one essay question from a choice of two on their studied modern prose or drama text'

findings.claim: He wrote Animal Farm in 1945 specifically to show how Stalin had corrupted the ideals of the Russian Revolution.
findings.truth: Orwell wrote the novella between November 1943 and February 1944. It was published on 17 August 1945.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Farm (composition Nov 1943 - Feb 1944; published 17 Aug 1945, Secker and Warburg)

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5 are auto-generated clozes built from a run-on of a heading and body text: answers 'Russian' and 'Anger'.
findings.truth: Neither card is answerable as written and neither question opens with What/Which/Who/When/Name. Replaced with two clean questions on Russia and Tsar Nicholas II.
findings.evidence: raw/L01.txt flashcard_questions[3], [4]

findings.claim: 'All animals are equal, but some are more equal than others.' (also in lesson 2 practice[4].marks and lesson 5 practice[2].marks)
findings.truth: The commandment reads 'ALL ANIMALS ARE EQUAL BUT SOME ANIMALS ARE MORE EQUAL THAN OTHERS'. The word 'animals' is dropped in three places. Lessons 8 and 10 already quote it correctly.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 10

findings.claim: Euphemism: calling self-interest 'preserving our health'.
findings.truth: Squealer's words are 'Our sole object in taking these things is to preserve our health.'
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 3

findings.claim: taking the puppies away 'to educate them himself'
findings.truth: Not Orwell's words. Ch 3 reads 'saying that he would make himself responsible for their education'.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 3

findings.claim: He is described charging 'straight for Jones' (also quoted as the stimulus of practice question 1 and analysed word by word in its mark scheme).
findings.truth: Fabricated quotation. Ch 4 reads 'Without halting for an instant, Snowball flung his fifteen stone against Jones's legs.' A student memorising 'charged straight for Jones' would quote words that are not in the novella.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 4

findings.claim: they spread rumours about the farm - 'the animals practised tyranny against their own kind'
findings.truth: Fabricated quotation. The Ch 4 rumours are that the animals 'practised cannibalism, tortured one another with red-hot horseshoes, and had their females in common'. The word 'tyranny' never appears in that passage.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 4

findings.claim: reflects the complex relationship between the Western world and the USSR during the Cold War
findings.truth: Anachronism. The novella was written in 1943-44 and published in August 1945; the Cold War is later. Ch 4 allegorises Western hostility to the Soviet state after 1917. Fixed in the same sentence as F10.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Farm

findings.claim: He tells the animals that Snowball was 'always a traitor'... When Boxer objects, saying 'He fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed'... the three dogs growled so threateningly that Boxer falls silent.
findings.truth: Three errors. 'Always a traitor' is not in the book (Ch 5 has 'no better than a criminal'). In Ch 5 the objection is made by an unnamed animal ('said somebody'); Boxer's objection is in Ch 7. And Ch 5 says the animals 'accepted his explanation without further questions', not that Boxer fell silent.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 5 and Ch 7

findings.claim: Most animals accept this explanation without question - only Boxer hesitates.
findings.truth: No animal hesitates. Ch 6 reads 'The animals were shocked beyond measure to learn that even Snowball could be guilty of such an action.' Boxer's doubt about Snowball comes in Ch 7.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 6

findings.claim: Card 4 is an auto-generated cloze from a collapsible heading, answer 'Context'.
findings.truth: Unanswerable. Replaced with a question on Alexei Stakhanov.
findings.evidence: raw/L06.txt flashcard_questions[3]

findings.truth: Ch 8 reads 'A mighty cry for vengeance went up'.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 8

findings.claim: 'without cause' (Ch.7) - repeated in lesson 10 content_html, the memorisation list of commandment changes.
findings.truth: The altered Sixth Commandment is read out to Clover by Muriel at the start of Chapter 8, not Chapter 7. Chapter 7 is the executions.

findings.claim: <dfn ... data-def='A person whose trade is the disposal of dead or unwanted animals...'>Benjamin</dfn>
findings.truth: The glossary tooltip for a knacker is attached to the character's name, so a student hovering 'Benjamin' is told Benjamin is a slaughterer. Moved onto 'Horse Slaughterer' in the van lettering, keeping the attribute verbatim.
findings.evidence: raw/L09.txt content_html

findings.claim: The pigs... enjoy increasing privileges: ... and the right to walk on their hind legs within the farmhouse.
findings.truth: The pigs first walk on their hind legs in Chapter 10, which is the climax of the novella. The Chapter 9 privileges are beer, a schoolroom for the piglets, and green ribbons on their tails on Sundays.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 9 and Ch 10

findings.claim: Chapter Nine catalogues the pigs' privileges... beer rations, separate schooling for piglets, reduced working hours.
findings.truth: No reduction in the pigs' hours is mentioned; the pigs never do field work anyway. The third privilege is green ribbons on Sundays.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 9

findings.claim: The farm now 'possessed' three horses, a cart, and a plough
findings.truth: Ch 10 reads 'The farm possessed three horses now besides Clover' and, separately, 'the farm possessed a threshing machine and a hay elevator of its own'. There is no cart or plough in the list; Whymper buys a dogcart.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 10

findings.claim: Every lesson labels two practice questions '8 marks - Extract Analysis' and several stems read 'Starting with this extract from Chapter X... in this extract' (20 questions across the unit).
findings.truth: The modern prose or drama question prints no extract and is closed book, so 'extract' misnames the task. BUT the 4/8/12 ladder with these exact labels is the house scaffold in all five Unity English Literature units (a-christmas-carol, macbeth, power-and-conflict, unseen-poetry), so a rename is a corpus decision, not an Animal Farm fix. Options: (a) leave the ladder and accept it as a practice scaffold; (b) rename '8 marks - Extract Analysis' to '8 marks - Quotation Analysis' and change 'this extract' to 'this moment' across the Unity English Literature corpus. Recommendation: (b), but as one corpus-wide sweep. The free-tier english-literature-aqa animal-farm unit already uses '30+4 marks - Modern Text Essay' labels instead.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md; scripts/_retrofc/units/english-literature@unity__*/raw/L01.txt

findings.claim: the pigs need comfort to do their 'brainwork.'
findings.truth: 'Brainwork' as a single word is not in the novella. Ch 3 has 'We pigs are brainworkers' and Ch 6 has 'the pigs, who were the brains of the farm'. The sense is right, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 3 and Ch 6

findings.claim: For the first time in the novel, Benjamin breaks his silence and cries out
findings.truth: Benjamin speaks earlier (Ch 3, 'Donkeys live a long time'). Ch 9 says it was the first time anyone had seen him excited or seen him gallop. The point being made still stands, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia text of Animal Farm (http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100011.txt), grepped in a scratch dir, not saved to the repo, Ch 3 and Ch 9

findings.claim: The personification of the dogs as blood-crazed killers
findings.truth: Going mad after tasting blood is animal behaviour, not a human quality, so 'personification' is loose terminology here. Not worth an edit, but a teacher may want to correct it.
findings.evidence: raw/L07.txt content_html, narration block n7

summary: 27 findings across all 10 lessons: 4 HIGH (two fabricated quotations in lesson 4, a false claim that the exam prints an extract, and a knacker tooltip attached to the character name Benjamin), 17 MEDIUM, 6 LOW. 23 findings are fixed by 35 surgical edits; 1 ADJUDICATE (the unit-wide Extract Analysis practice labels, which are a Unity-wide house scaffold); 3 NOTE. Every quotation was checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg Australia text of the novella, every exam claim against the spec, and every allegory claim against Wikipedia. All 50 knowledge-check answer keys are correct.
